plan: [In a sealed-bid second-price auction, truthful bidding (bid = my private value) is a dominant strategy regardless of others' beliefs. My value is $9, so I will bid $9. This maximizes expected profit: if I win I pay the second-highest bid (≤ my value), yielding nonnegative surplus; if I lose I pay nothing. Ties are random and have negligible effect on expected payoff.]

[This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. Truthful bidding (bidding my value) is a dominant strategy for each rational bidder and maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Other bidders are rational and will anticipate this. To maximize long-run profit (and in this single round), I will bid my private value of $40. Tie-breaks are random; bids must be in $0.1 increments, so I submit 40.0 if necessary.]

[In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding my true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Other rational bidders will also bid their values; truthful bidding maximizes my expected surplus (win when value exceeds competitors' bids and pay the second-highest). Bidding higher risks overpaying; bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. Therefore bid my private value $32.]
